questions.question: A can finish (2)/(5) of a task in 12 days and B can finish(2)/(3) of the same task in 30 days. They work together for 10 days. C alone complete the remaining task in 16 days, B and C together will complete (4)/(5) of the same task in:
questions.solution:
**Given:**

A can finish (2)/(5) of a task in 12 days and B can finish(2)/(3) of the same task in 30 days.

**Calculation:**

A's 1 day's work = 2/5 × 1/12 = 1/30

B's 1 day's work = 2/3 × 1/30 = 1/45

(A + B)'s 1 days work = 1/30 + 1/45 = 1/18

(A + B)'s 10 days work = 10 × 1/18 = 5/9

Remaining work = 1 - 5/9 = 4/9

C's 1 day's work = 4/9 × 1/16 = 1/36

(B + C)'s 1 day's work = 1/45 + 1/36 = 9/180 = 1/20

**∴ B and C will complete 4/5th work in = 4/5 × 20 = 16 days.**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] __Important Points__** 

Time taken by person to complete a/b fraction of work = a/b × (Number of days in which person alone can complete work)

questions.question: A is 20% more than B, B is 10% less than C and C is 15% more than D. Which of the following is true?
The average of seven consecutive odd numbers (in increasing order) is k. If the next four consecutive odd numbers are included, then the average of all the number is:
questions.solution:
**Formula:**

Average = Total sum/Number of elements

**Calculation:**

Let seven consecutive odd numbers be a, a + 2, a + 4, a + 6, a + 8, a + 10 and a + 12

Accordingly,

Sum of the odd numbers = Average × Total number

Let a be the first odd number then, 

a + a + 2 + a + 4 + a + 6 + a + 8 + a + 10 + a + 12 = k × 7

⇒ 7a + 42 = 7k

⇒ a + 6 = k

⇒ a = k - 6

New average = [(a + 14 + a + 16 + a + 18 + a + 20) + (7a + 42)]/(7 + 4) = (11a + 110)/11 = a + 10

**∴ New average = k - 6 + 10 = k + 4**

Subtracting,

In 4 years interest is (8256 - 5952) = 2304

questions.question: The 10-digit number 90457416xy is divisible by 9, and x - y = 3. What is the value of (5x + 3y)?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

90457416xy is divisible by 9 

x - y = 3

**Concept Used:**

If sum of all digits of a number is divisible by 9 then the number should also be divisible by 9

**Calculation:**

(9 + 0 + 4 + 5 + 7 + 4 + 1 + 6 + x + y)/9 = (36 + x + y)/9

For 10 digit number to divisible by 9 then (36 + x + y) is completely divisible by 9.

⇒ x + y = 9

Also given x - y = 3

Solving,

x = 6 and y = 3

5x + 3y = 5 × 6 + 3 × 3 = 39

**∴ Required value of (5x + 3y) is 39.**

questions.question: The average of 13 number is 48.5. The average of the first five numbers is 56.4 and that of the last nine numbers is 45.6. What is the 5th number?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Total sum of 13 numbers = 13 × 48.5 = 630.5

**Formula:**

Average = Sum of numbers/Total numbers

**Calculation:**

Total sum of first 5 numbers = 5 × 56.4 = 282

Total sum of last 9 numbers = 9 × 45.6 = 410.4

**∴ 5th number = (282 + 410.4) - 630.5 = 61.9**

questions.question: Suresh loses 15% when he sells his computer for Rs. 17,000. If he sells it for Rs. 20,448, then his loss/profit percentage is:
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Selling price = Rs.17000

Loss % = 17%

**Formula:**

Selling price = cost price × (100 - loss %)/100

**Calculation:**

Cost price = 17000 × 100/85 = Rs.20000

**∴ Profit percentage = (20448 - 20000)/20000 × 100 = 2.24%**

questions.question: Pipes A and B can fill a tank in 18 minutes and 27 minutes, respectively. C is an outlet pipe. When A, B and C are opened together, the empty tank is completely filled in 54 minutes. Pipe C alone can empty the full tank in:
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Pipes A and B can fill a tank in 18 minutes and 27 minutes, respectively.

When A, B and C are opened together, the empty tank is completely filled in 54 minutes.

**Calculation:**

Pipe A's 1 minute's work = 1/18

Pipe B's 1 minute's work = 1/27

Let pipe C's 1 minute's work be 1/C.

⇒ (1/18 + 1/27) - 1

questions.question: The ratio of the present ages of A and B is 5 : 6. Eight years ago, the ratio of their ages was 4 : 5. What will be the ratio of the ages of A and B after 8 years from now?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

The ratio of the present ages of A and B is 5 : 6.

Eight years ago, the ratio of their ages was 4 : 5.

**Calculation:**

Let present ages of A and B be 5a and 6a respectively.

8 year ago age of A was (5a - 8) years

8 years ago age of B was (6a - 8) years

Accordingly,

(5a - 8) : (6a - 8) = 4 : 5

⇒ (5a - 8)/(6a - 8) = 4/5

**⇒ **25a - 40 = 24a - 32

**⇒ **a = 8

Present age of A and B is 40 years and 48 years respectively

**∴ Required ratio = (40 + 8) : (48 + 8) = 48 : 56 = 6 : 7**

The value of ((1)/(2) of 1 (1)/(2)) ÷ (3 frac 1 2 - 1 frac 1 4) of 3/2 - 3/2 div 9/4 + 4/3 is:
questions.solution:
**Concept Used:**

Follow the BODMAS rule according to the table given below:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4674d8914559775faa130de47444b599d5acddd541c3cfae2a6936129288b871.png] 

**Calculation:**

((1)/(2) of 1 (1)/(2)) ÷ (3 frac 1 2 - 1 frac 1 4) of 3/2 - 3/2 div 9/4 + 4/3

⇒ (1/2 × 3/2) ÷ (7/2 - 5/4) × 3/2 - 3/2 ÷ 9/4 + 4/3

questions.question: In a class of 45 students, the ratio of the number of boys and girls is 4 : 5. The average score of boys in mathematics is 78. If the average score of all the students in the class in mathematics is 76, then what is the average score of girls in mathematics?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Boy : girl = 4 : 5

**Calculation:**

Let number of boys and girls in a class be 4a and 5a respectively.

Total score of boys = 78 × 4a

Total score of class = 76 × 9a

Total score of girls = 76 × 9a - 78 × 4a = 372a

**∴ Average score of girls = 372a/5a = 74.4**

questions.question: In a test consisting of 120 questions, a candidate correctly answers 60% of the first 90 questions. What percentage of the remaining questions does he need to answer correctly so that his answers to 55% of the total questions in the test are correct?
questions.solution:
**Calculation:**

Let percentage questions required be a.

⇒ 60/100 × 90 + a/100 × 30 = 55/100 × 120

⇒ 54 + 0.3a = 66

⇒ a = 40

**∴ 40% of remaining questions should answer correctly.**

questions.question: What is the compound interest on a sum of Rs. 13,000 at 15% p.a. in 2 years, if the interest is compounded 8-monthly?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Rate per 8-month cycle = 15% × (8/12) = 10%.

Number of cycles in 2 years (24 months) = 24 ÷ 8 = 3.

Effective compound interest rate for 3 cycles at 10% = 33.1%.

Compound Interest = 33.1% of Rs. 13,000 = 33.1 × 130 = Rs. 4,303.

**∴ The correct answer is Rs. 4,303.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Principal (P) = Rs. 13,000

Rate of Interest (R) = 15% p.a.

Time (T) = 2 years = 24 months

 
• 
• 
• 13000 14300 15730 17303 
 +10% (8 mo) 
 +10% (8 mo) 
 +10% (8 mo) 0 months 8 months 16 months 24 months Total CI = 17303 − 13000 = 4303 

**Formula Used:**

Amount (A) = P × [1 + (r / 100)]ⁿ

Where r = rate per compounding period, and n = total number of periods.

**Calculations:**

⇒ Rate for 8 months (r) = 15 × (8 / 12) = 10% per period

⇒ Number of periods (n) = 24 ÷ 8 = 3

⇒ A = 13000 × [1 + (10 / 100)]³

⇒ A = 13000 × (11 / 10)³

⇒ A = 13000 × (1331 / 1000)

⇒ A = 13 × 1331 = 17,303

⇒ Compound Interest (CI) = A − P

⇒ CI = 17303 − 13000 = Rs. 4,303

**∴ The correct answer is Rs. 4,303.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Effective Rate Method

For 2 consecutive periods, effective CI rate = x + y + (xy / 100)%. Applying this successively for 3 cycles of 10% gives 33.1% direct compound interest.

Custom Compounding Periods

If compounded 'm' monthly, Rate = R × (m / 12) and Number of cycles = (Time in months) ÷ m.

Successive Ratio Trick

For 3 compounding periods, CI can also be rapidly calculated using the 3 : 3 : 1 ratio trick applied to the consecutive percentage values of the principal.

questions.question: The cost price of a shirt is Rs. 262.40, At what price should it be marked so as to gain 14% after allowing a 18% discount on the market price?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Cost price = Rs.262.40

**Formula:**

Selling price = cost price × (profit % + 100)/100

**Calculation:**

Let the marked price of a shirt be Rs.a

Selling price after discount = a × (100 - 18)/100 = Rs.82a/100

Accordingly,

82a/100 = 262.40 × (100 + 14)/100

⇒ 82a/100 = 29991.36/100

⇒ a = 364.80

**∴ The marked price of a shirt is Rs.364.80.**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/0a6c2db12945bba9d674d33112fce66b07f00093d75dae93749f9bdb7bd34e7a.png] __Hint__** 

Selling price after discount = Marked price × (100 - discount %)/100

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

{Marked price(MP) over Cost price (CP)} = {{100 + Profit \%} over {100 - discount \%}}

⇒ MP/262.40 = (100 + 14)/(100 - 18)

⇒ MP/262.40 = 114/82

⇒ MP = (114 × 262.40)/82

⇒ MP = 364.80

∴ The marked price of a shirt is Rs.364.80.

questions.question: The sides of a triangular field are 56 m, 90 m and 106 m. The cost of levelling the field at Rs. 6.80 per m² is:
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Sides = 56m, 90m and 106m

**Calculation:**

The triangular filed is a right angle field as it satisfies pythagoras theorem,

Area of triangular field = 1/2 × 56 × 90 = 2520 cm²

∴ cost of levelling field = 2520 × 6.80

questions.question: The cost price of an article A is 20% more than that of B. A is sold for Rs. 1,800 at a loss of 20% and B is sold such that there is a profit of 20% on both A and B together. The selling price of B is:
questions.solution:
**Given:**

The cost price of the article A is 20% more than that of B.

 A is sold for Rs. 1,800 at a loss of 20%

**Calculation:**

Let cost price of B be Rs.a.

Cost price of A = Rs.120a/100

 A is sold for Rs. 1,800 at a loss of 20%

⇒ Cost price of A is 1800 × 100/80

Accordingly,

120a/100 = 1800 × 100/80

⇒ a = Rs.1875

Cost price of A = 1875 × 120/100 = Rs.2250

Total cost price of A and B = 2250 + 1875 = Rs.4125

Total selling price = 4125 × 120/100 = Rs.4950

**∴ Selling price of B = 4950 - 1800 = Rs.3150**

questions.question: Rina bought 24 kg sugar for Rs. 1,056. She sold it at a profit equal to the selling price of 4 kg of it. The selling price of sugar, per kg, was:
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Cost price of 24 kg sugar = Rs.1056

**Formula:**

Profit = selling price - cost price

**Calculation:**

Let selling price of sugar per kg be Rs.a

⇒ 4a = 24a - 1056

⇒ a = 52.80

**∴ The selling price of a sugar per kg is Rs.52.80**

questions.question: The price of wheat, per kg, is increased by 17.5% and the quantity of wheat bought is decreased by 10%. What is the percentage change in the amount spent on wheat?
questions.solution:
**Calculation:**

Let previously the price of wheat be Rs.a

New price of wheat = a × (117.5/100) = Rs.4.7a/4

Quantity of wheat initially bought be m.

New quantity of wheat bought = 90m/100 = 9m/10

Previously, the total price of wheat was am.

Then,

Amount spent increase = (4.7m/4 × 9m/10 - am)/am × 100

⇒ 5.75%

**∴ 5.75% increase in amount.**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] __Alternate Method__**Another simple and short solution for this type of question is as follows:

Percentage Change in the amount spent = Increase in price × decrease in consumption/buying 

Percentage Change in the amount spent = 117.5/100 × 90/100

⇒ 47/40 × 9/10 = 423/400

∴ Percentage change in the amount spent = 23/400 × 100 = 5.75%

questions.question: An article is sold for Rs. 1,683, after giving three successive discounts of 15%, 10% and 12% on its marked price. The marked price of the article is:
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Selling price = Rs.1683

**Concept Used:**

If a%, b% are two different discounts then the selling price is calculated as -

Selling price = marked price × (100 - a)/100 × (100 - b)/100

**Calculation:**

Marked price × 85/100 × 90/100 × 88/100 = 1683

**∴ Marked price = Rs.2500**

questions.question: A sum amounts to Rs. 6,050 in 2 years and to Rs. 6,655 in 3 years at a certain rate percentage p.a. when the interest is compounded yearly. What is the simple interest on a sum of Rs. 6,000 at the same rate for 5(3)/(4) years?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

A sum amounts to Rs. 6,050 in 2 years and to Rs. 6,655 in 3 years at a certain rate percentage p.a. when the interest is compounded yearly.

**Formula:**

Let P = Principal, R = rate of interest and N = time period

Simple interest = PNR/100

Compound interest = P(1 + R/100)ⁿ - P

questions.question: A train of length 218 m is running at 60 km/h. In what time (in seconds) will it cross a platform of length 282 m?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Length of train = 218m

speed of train = 60kmph = 60 × 5/18 = 50/3 m/s

Length of the platform = 282 m

**Concept Used:**

Time taken to cross a platform = (length of train + length of the platform)/speed of the train

**Calculation:**

Time required = (218 + 282)/(50/3) = 30 seconds

**∴ In 30 second the train will cross the platform of length 282m.**

questions.question: If a + b + c = 7 and a³ + b³ + c³ - 3abc = 175, then what is the value of ab + bc + ca?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

⇒ a + b + c = 7

⇒ a³ + b³ + c³ - 3abc = 175

**Formula Used:**

a3 + b3 + c3 - 3abc = (a + b + c)(a² + b² + c² - ab - bc - ca)

(a + b + c)2 = (a2 + b2 + c2 + 2ab + 2bc + 2ca)

**Calculation:**

(a + b + c)² = (a² + b² + c² + 2ab + 2bc + 2ca)

⇒ 49 - 2(ab + bc + ca) = (a² + b² + c²) ----(1)

Now,

a³ + b³ + c³ - 3abc = (a + b + c) (a² + b² + c² - ab - bc - ca)

⇒ 175 = 7 × [49 - 2(ab + bc + ca) - ab - bc - ca]

⇒ 3(ab + bc + ca) = 24

⇒ ab + bc + ca = 8

**∴ Required value of ab + bc + ca is 8**
